title.narrative: Nui and Niutao Islands Boat Harbour Development - Tuvalu - Transport

description.narrative:
Australia, through the Australian Infrastructure Financing Facility for the Pacific (AIFFP), has provided a grant package to the Government of Tuvalu alongside support from the Asian Development Bank for the construction of work boat harbours on two outer islands. The works include new wharf facilities and supporting landside infrastructure at Niutao and Nui islands, with the design and construction of the harbours considering climate change mitigation and adaptations measures.
Many island communities in Tuvalu are dependent on shipping for food and for access to essential services and supplies. The project increases the availability and reliability of transport options for Nui and Niutao communities. Villages and households in more remote communities will have improved access to markets and services, schools and health services. In addition, the project includes support to the Government of Tuvalu to improve maritime safety and operational practices at the two harbours.

description.narrative: In 2024, the Australian Infrastructure Financing Facility for the Pacific (AIFFP) supported a key infrastructure project aimed at improving boat harbours across Tuvalu. AIFFP has placed strong emphasis on local and regional workforce participation. 30 per cent of the workforce—an average of eight out of 30 workers across 2024—were Tuvaluan. These workers were selected in partnership with government and community leaders, ensuring alignment with local skills and availability. ‍ The project also supported broader regional engagement, with Pacific expatriates from Fiji making up around 40 per cent of the workforce. This approach helped extend economic benefits beyond Tuvalu, contributing to regional development and cooperation. ‍ Importantly, the project created new opportunities for local women. At the Niutao Island Boat Harbour site, female participation reached 20 per cent of the local workforce—double the target rate of 10 per cent. This milestone reflects a growing commitment to gender inclusion in infrastructure delivery. ‍ Through this project, AIFFP has demonstrated how targeted workforce strategies can support local employment, regional collaboration, and inclusive development outcomes.

title.narrative: Climate adaptation, mitigation, environment and biodiversity

description.narrative: Tuvalu, one of the world’s most climate-vulnerable nations, is charting a new course toward resilient maritime infrastructure. With investment through the Australian Infrastructure Financing Facility for the Pacific (AIFFP), in partnership with the Asian Development Bank and the Government of Tuvalu, the Enhancing Boat Harbours project is ensuring Nui and Niutao island harbours can withstand increasingly adverse weather events now and in the future. ‍ The new harbour at Nui has integrated future climate projections—rising sea levels, cyclones, and coastal erosion—into every aspect of its construction. Innovations such as raised foreshores, rock bag coastal protection, and duckbill valves to prevent flooding, and relocated and elevated facilities, will ensure long-term safety and functionality. ‍ Beyond infrastructure, the project strengthens Tuvalu’s disaster response, economic stability, and local capacity. Collaboration with international experts has empowered Tuvaluans with advanced coastal protection knowledge. ‍ Project Manager Mr Vete Sakaio emphasises the importance of forward-thinking “We’re not only building for today, but for future generations.” ‍ Nui Harbour is more than a harbour—it’s a lifeline. It now connects communities to markets, schools, and healthcare, while standing strong against the rising tide of climate change.
